captions.detailed: A 3D-printable parametric bridge test structure, designed to evaluate bridging performance. It consists of a long, thin, raised horizontal rectangular bridge span supported at both ends by angled, wedge-like pillars. Each support pillar is integrated with a thin, rounded rectangular brim (or adhesion pad) at its base to ensure stable bed adhesion during printing.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric 3D printer bridge test structure in OpenSCAD. The model should include a thin horizontal bridge span suspended between two angled support pillars, with customizable parameters for bridge length, width, height, thickness, and slicer settings like extrusion width and layer height. Additionally, include a rounded brim at the base of each support for print bed adhesion.
captions.factory: The code defines two main modules: Support() and bridge(). The Support() module uses a difference operation to cut a rectangular cube at an angle calculated dynamically using trigonometry, creating a wedge-shaped pillar; it then uses a minkowski() sum of a flat cube and a cylinder to generate a rounded brim at the base. The bridge() module uses a union of a horizontal cube representing the bridge span and a 3D text label on top. The final assembly translates the supports to both ends of the bridge (rotating one support 180 degrees) and places the main bridge span across them.
